cluster_summary: This cluster comprises vulnerabilities resulting from insecure defaults in XML processing. The majority involve XML parsers that do not disable DTD processing or external entity resolution, enabling XXE attacks. Other issues include insecure deserialization via XMLDecoder, XSLT extension function abuse, resource exhaustion from missing EOF checks, variable interpolation leaking system properties, and NTLM credential exposure through namespace URI resolution.
guideline_text: Trace lower-privilege script, template, macro, plugin, or API callers that can invoke privileged server-side capabilities into server-side include, template rendering, servlet dispatch, raw object access, internal file reads, or privileged framework APIs. Report code paths where a higher privilege check is not enforced at the API entry point before exposing the server-side capability. Confirm that the guard is enforced before the sensitive effect and remains bound to the same resource, principal, destination, or object that the effect uses. Treat this as a reusable mechanism-level pattern derived from 1 historical CVE example(s), not as a project-specific signature. A safe implementation should check the required higher privilege at the exposed API boundary and return no sensitive result when the caller lacks that privilege.

mechanism.missing_guard: a higher privilege check is not enforced at the API entry point before exposing the server-side capability
mechanism.name: privileged server-side capability exposed to lower privilege context
mechanism.sink_shape: server-side include, template rendering, servlet dispatch, raw object access, internal file reads, or privileged framework APIs
mechanism.source_shape: lower-privilege script, template, macro, plugin, or API callers that can invoke privileged server-side capabilities
mechanism.typical_fix: check the required higher privilege at the exposed API boundary and return no sensitive result when the caller lacks that privilege

sub_patterns.fix_strategy: Explicitly disable DTD declarations and external entity resolution by setting appropriate features on the parser factory (e.g., disallow-doctype-decl, external-general-entities=false, external-parameter-entities=false, FEATURE_SECURE_PROCESSING, ACCESS_EXTERNAL_DTD empty) or by providing a restrictive EntityResolver that blocks external resources.
sub_patterns.name: Missing secure parser configuration against external entity resolution
sub_patterns.root_cause: XML parser factories (DocumentBuilderFactory, SAXParserFactory, XMLInputFactory, SAXBuilder, etc.) are instantiated with default settings that permit DTD processing and external entity resolution. The code fails to disable these unsafe features before parsing untrusted XML input.
